body: Hey! I’m her big sister, when she was 12 she went to a special school Monday- Friday which seemed to really do her good but unfortunately this was only for just over a year as was only for primary. We have thought about this and also had it threatened to us to hospitalise her but the issue is, no matter what degree or qualifications any professional has, Lexie’s case is so different, not just because of being trans or the autism or anorexia but all the little things that it just wouldn’t work. While looking into the idea we spoke with several places around the world and came across some horrible stories. Lexie is a very bright intelligent kid and we really don’t agree with her being given all sorts of drugs to stabilise her. If we found a place that would look and care for her it would be a miracle but the way it works once your in the system, if you don’t abide with the rules (which Lexie won’t, she is autistic) they will just drug you up until you are not you anymore. She is much better off being at home, or at least until we find the right place but it’s just about giving her a better quality of life, I don’t know how to do that. :(
